clue.text: Make a song about cold and damp foreign currency

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the singing word wraps the weather word

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
a chill is a raw, cold and damp spell

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about a chilly, wet stash of money brought back from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' looks like the idiom for complaining, but SING is placed about CHILL. The schilling was Austria's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was the national money of Austria, a currency foreign to British readers.

clue.text: American biscuit firm that is inwardly all right

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OK means all right
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An American biscuit company whose inner workings are perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a small sweet baked biscuit is called a cookie.

clue.text: I'm not one to cause damage, apparently

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
something that is not one but two is a pair

explanation.surface: A harmless person protests that they are not the destructive type.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm not one' as I'M PAIR: a pair is what you have when there is not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or spoil it, doing it harm.

clue.text: Hidden talent redeployed

indicators.note: redeployed means the letters of talent are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A gift nobody had noticed is put to use somewhere new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but not yet visible or active, so concealed.

clue.text: Not expected to benefit from industry, as the railways are?

definitions.text: Not expected to benefit from industry, as the railways are?

parts.words: Not expected to benefit from industry, as the railways are?
parts.note: describes an enterprise run to provide a service, not to earn its owners money, with a dig at loss-making nationalised railways

explanation.surface: A grumble that state-run railways never pay their way.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was nationalised and famously ran at a loss, so the clue jokes that railways are run without profit in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A body that is not set up to earn a surplus for owners is described with this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Takes back what one has said about how pools winners come up on the treble chance?

definitions.text: Takes back what one has said
how pools winners come up on the treble chance?

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a boast about how football pools winners hit the jackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British betting game on match results; the treble chance paid out for predicting draws, so winners came up 'with draws'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back; on the treble chance football pools, winning coupons come up with score draws.

clue.text: Pip in the Ten District collecting impressions from home and abroad

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Pip in the Ten District collecting impressions from home and abroad': 'collecting impressions' defines stamp collecting, but 'Pip in the Ten District' gives none of the letters PHIL + AT + ELY and looks OCR-garbled beyond a few letters; no reprint found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Pip in the Ten District collecting impressions from home and abroad

clue.text: Distinguished old Hungarian family curiously terse and ill-defined

indicators.note: curiously means the letters of terse are arranged in an odd new way

parts.note: something ill-defined is hazy, vague

explanation.surface: A noble Hungarian dynasty is described as oddly curt and vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges TERSE into ESTER, then HAZY follows. The Esterhazys were patrons of Haydn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Esterházy princes were a great Hungarian noble house, famous as patrons of the composer Haydn.

clue.text: In the south it used to be the life-blood of the Church

definitions.text: used to be the life-blood of the Church

indicators.note: In at the front means the later word it is placed within the other words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that in southern parts something once kept the Church alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start puts IT inside THE + S, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income was once paid to support the clergy, funding the parish church.

clue.text: Kind of talc from which teaspoons may be made

indicators.note: may be made means the letters of teaspoons can be built into something else

explanation.surface: Someone notes a mineral that spoons might be carved from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from which' is a link; 'may be made' rearranges TEASPOONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Steatite is a soft rock made largely of talc, used for carving.

clue.text: Gradually descend to procrastination?

explanation.surface: Someone slides slowly into the habit of putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a verb for the deed of procrastinating: to put a plan on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that slopes gently downward does this; and putting a matter aside to deal with later is the act of delay.

clue.text: He dreams one is turned on when change is about

indicators.note: about means the word for change goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turned means the little word is is flipped round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreamer gets excited whenever change is in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips IS into SI; I + SI + ON sits inside VARY, after its V.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is an idealist who imagines a better future, someone given to dreams.

clue.text: River fish landed outside a manger?

indicators.note: outside means the haul word goes around the river letter and the a

parts.note: the fish an angler has landed is the catch

explanation.surface: An angler's haul from the river is left lying around a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A cratch is an old word for a rack or crib holding fodder for animals.

clue.text: We are about to strike a new deal for the paint industry, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the word we goes around the word for strike

parts.note: to strike is to hit

indicators.note: new means the letters of deal are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A union says it is ready to strike for a better pay deal in the paint trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HIT inside WE; 'new' rearranges DEAL into LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic lead carbonate was long used as a white pigment in house paint.

clue.text: Sees Latin as a sine qua non

indicators.note: as here means the two words are recast as something else

explanation.surface: Someone regards Latin as indispensable, quoting a Latin phrase to prove it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' signals that SEES and LATIN together are recast, an unusual anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine qua non is Latin for a thing without which something cannot be, an indispensable requirement.

clue.text: Easily the best student in the astronomy class?

definitions.text: Easily the best student in the astronomy class?

parts.words: Easily the best student in the astronomy class?
parts.note: the top pupil of a class is called by a phrase that, in an astronomy lesson, sounds like a learner of the stars

explanation.surface: Praise for the outstanding scholar in a stargazing course.
explanation.definitionFit: The most brilliant learner in a class is its outstanding scholar, here punning on stars studied in astronomy.

clue.text: Small creature that lives a double life

definitions.text: Small creature that lives a double life

parts.words: Small creature that lives a double life
parts.note: an amphibian lives both in water and on land, the double life of the Greek amphibios

explanation.surface: A tiny animal is said to lead a secret double existence.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small amphibian living both in water and on land.

clue.text: When one may expect to get a letter from Greece

definitions.text: When one may expect to get

explanation.surface: Someone wonders when post from Greece will turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: The estimated time of arrival tells you when to expect to arrive; and eta is the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Extremely low digit

parts.note: the lowest of the body's digits are those on the foot, at the very bottom

explanation.surface: A remark about a very small number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' suggests a number, but it is a finger or its counterpart on the foot, the lowest on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits of the foot are the lowest-placed digits of the body.

clue.text: Steps embarked upon with some reluctance at a social gathering?

definitions.text: Steps embarked upon with some reluctance at a social gathering?

parts.words: Steps embarked upon with some reluctance at a social gathering?
parts.note: dance steps begun shyly at a party, read as a named ballroom dance

explanation.surface: A shy guest edges onto the dance floor at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ballroom dance with pauses in its steps, read here as dancing with reluctance.

clue.text: Was no faster returning 17 down

indicators.note: returning means the answer to the cross-referenced light is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 17 down, the Greek letter

explanation.surface: Someone was no quicker on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' is not quicker but one who fasts: someone who ate was not fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who had a meal was not going without food, so not a faster.

clue.text: They hold an alternative view of the underlying principles

indicators.note: hold means the word they contains the word for an alternative

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Some people take a different view of the fundamentals.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of principles explaining something, or a held view about it, is its rationale or hypothesis.

clue.text: Sort of person to whom a youngster may go in sore distress

definitions.text: Sort of person to whom a youngster may go

indicators.note: distress, read as a verb, means the letters of in sore are disturbed

explanation.surface: A child in pain runs to an older person for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: An older, more experienced person is the one a youngster turns to for help.

clue.text: Turnip plants climbing round thwarts

indicators.note: round means the reversed plants word goes around the other piece
climbing in a down light means the word for plants is read upwards

parts.note: sets are young plants such as onion sets
read as turn-ip: IP turned round gives PI

explanation.surface: Turnip seedlings growing upwards foil someone's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Turnip' as TURN IP to get PI; 'climbing' reverses SETS to STES, and PI goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To spite someone can mean to frustrate or deliberately hinder them.

clue.text: What a lady will go to a top stylist for?

definitions.text: What a lady will go to a top stylist for?

parts.words: What a lady will go to a top stylist for?
parts.note: a top stylist is a hairdresser, who styles the top of the head

explanation.surface: A question about why a woman visits a fashionable salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A styled arrangement of the hair is what a salon visit produces.

clue.text: Reconciliation officer who works behind the scenes?

explanation.surface: A peace-broker who operates out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up is to reconcile, so a reconciler is a make-up man; and a theatre cosmetics artist works backstage.

clue.text: Free to make more of a habit?

definitions.text: to make more of a habit?

explanation.surface: Someone at liberty to indulge a habit further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' is the robe worn by a monk or nun, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to free; and letting out the seams of a garment, such as a monk's habit, enlarges it.

clue.text: It's not usual among colliers or clergymen, for instance

indicators.note: among means the shuffled piece is placed inside the word for colliers

parts.note: colliers are coal miners

indicators.note: not usual means the letters of it's are set out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as its letters, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A remark that something is rare among coal miners or churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usual' rearranges ITS into IST, which goes inside MINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergymen are examples of people who minister to a congregation.

clue.text: Is after a swift horse that can climb over rocks, maybe

definitions.text: that can climb over rocks, maybe

indicators.note: after means the word is follows the horse word

parts.note: the Arab is a fast breed of horse

explanation.surface: A quick horse that is able to scramble over rocky ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse misleads: the thing that climbs over rocks is a rock-cress plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabis, rock cress, is a low plant that spreads over rocks in rock gardens.

clue.text: Bellicose strike leader?

parts.note: not a union leader calling a walkout but a warlike party who strikes the first blow

explanation.surface: A militant trade union boss leading a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: The party that attacks first, starting a fight or war, is the attacker who began it.
